concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a citizen, who legally belongs to a country, from a resident who only lives there.
Explain citizenship as both a legal identity and a social responsibility involving active participation.
Identify the laws that set the rules for gaining or losing Indian citizenship.

topics.title: What Are Rights? Fundamental Rights and the Right to Equality

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why only claims that support the wellbeing and dignity of all count as rights.
Identify the six categories of Fundamental Rights and that they can be enforced in courts.
Distinguish equality from equity and relate the right to equality to non-discrimination.

topics.title: Right to Freedom, Right to Life and Right against Exploitation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the right to freedom comes with reasonable restrictions.
Describe the right to life as the right to live with dignity, including livelihood, health and a clean environment.
Apply the protections against child labour, forced labour and trafficking to real situations.

topics.title: Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights and Constitutional Remedies

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the freedom to choose, practise and share religion and the neutrality of state-run schools.
Describe how cultural and educational rights protect minorities' language, script and institutions.
Evaluate why the right to constitutional remedies is called the heart and soul of the Constitution.

topics.title: Duties: Fundamental Duties and Their Link with Rights

concepts.learning_objective: Recall when and how Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution.
Identify the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A from everyday examples.
Explain why rights and duties are two sides of the same coin and how they differ in enforcement.
Define discrimination and explain how it harms individuals and society.
Distinguish visible from invisible discrimination and explain why the latter is hard to penalise.
Recognise how Savitribai Phule and Anandibai Joshi fought discrimination.
Explain inclusion as making everyone feel welcomed, respected and given equal access.
Suggest practical steps that remove barriers to participation in school and society.
